objective: Review the first scoped sidecar build/run/compare result after the accepted native-parser handoff-contract-to-operator-plan execution boundary, accept only the narrow coverage-output-equivalence result, and select a definition gate for the true native Verilator command path without claiming native option support, timing, arbitrary filelists, automatic allocation, runtime/ABI change, or raw full-state equality.

review_decision.reason: The run validates exactly the reviewed sidecar execution boundary: it used accepted ready operator-plan metadata, a reviewed or regenerated seven-stage sidecar plan, generated reports and artifacts only under generated-output directories, and passed coverage_output_equivalence for the declared output words on the scoped pulp_ita_mha 64x1 run.
review_decision.weakest_point: The run command is still the existing template runner, not a real Verilator native option invocation. The result can therefore prove that the sidecar execution stages work for the reviewed metadata boundary, but it cannot prove a direct Verilator command path, arbitrary filelist dependency inference, automatic optimal GPU allocation, timing or speedup, runtime/ABI changes, or raw full-state equality.
accepted_because: the source run gate is downstream of the accepted execution-boundary review
the run used the tracked template config/slice_launch_templates/pulp_ita_mha.json and shape 64x1
all seven reviewed sidecar stages are recorded in the accepted order
command_argv and handoff metadata remain preview/build metadata rather than direct native Verilator runtime evidence
generated evidence paths are under reports/ and artifacts/ and are not source of truth
coverage_output_equivalence passed with mismatch count 0 across 64 state pairs
raw full-state equality, timing, speedup, arbitrary RTL/filelist support, automatic allocation, runtime/ABI change, and production LLM-serving throughput remain explicit non-claims

selected_next_workstream.name: define_verilator_native_option_parser_direct_command_path_boundary_gate
selected_next_workstream.reason: After the sidecar execution run is accepted, the narrowest remaining blocker for Verilator-like usability is defining how an eventual native Verilator option invocation becomes the reviewed sidecar command path without over-reading command_argv metadata as runtime authority.
selected_next_workstream.timing_not_selected_first: The source run deliberately does not promote timing or speedup evidence; timing should remain behind a separately defined measurement gate.
selected_next_workstream.arbitrary_filelist_not_selected_first: The run preserves parser filelists as build inputs only and does not infer source closure, so arbitrary filelist support requires a later source-boundary definition.
